Crème Brûlée

Mama's recipe, the one with the coffee in it. She used to make this for every birthday in the family, no exceptions, even the ones in July when nobody wanted their oven on.

Makes: 4 small custards

You need:
2 cups heavy cream
1/2 cup whole milk
2 tbsp instant espresso powder
5 egg yolks
1/2 cup white sugar
1 tsp vanilla
sugar for the tops, about 4 tbsp total

Heat the oven to 300 degrees. Warm the cream, milk and espresso powder together in a small pot, whisking so the powder dissolves, until it just starts to steam. Do not boil it.

In a separate bowl beat the yolks, sugar and vanilla together until it looks like pale ribbons.

Pour the hot cream mixture into the yolks a little at a time, whisking constantly. Strain it if you see any lumps of espresso powder.

Set four ramekins in a baking dish, fill with the custard, and pour boiling water into the dish until it comes about an inch up the sides.

About 45 minutes in the oven does it, the centers should still jiggle a little when you nudge the pan.

Take the ramekins out of the water right away so they stop cooking. Let them come to room temperature on the counter, then cover and put them in the fridge for at least 4 hours, longer is fine.

When you're ready to serve, pat the tops dry, dust with sugar, and either torch it or run it under the broiler for a minute or two, watching it the whole time so it doesn't burn.

Note from Mama: real espresso powder, not instant coffee granules, or it turns gritty.
